indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B6.2.1.4 Recognise water and air as important natural resources (indicator code printed as B6.2.1.5.2)

skills.description: Recognise that air is a mixture of gases including oxygen.
Explain that oxygen in the air is needed for burning.
Describe what happens when a candle is covered with a glass jar (the flame goes out because oxygen is used up).
State why air is important for burning and for life.
Predict what happens to a flame when air is removed or when fresh air is supplied.
Give everyday examples showing air supports burning (e.g. blowing on a fire, covering a fire to put it out).

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Air is not needed for burning.
A candle goes out in a jar because the jar is cold.
All gases in air support burning.
Blowing on a fire always puts it out.
Water puts out fire because it removes air only.
Air has no effect on fire.

questions.stem: What is air made of?
options: A mixture of gases including oxygen
questions.explanation: Air is a mixture of gases, including oxygen, nitrogen and carbon dioxide.
questions.misconception: Air is only oxygen.

questions.stem: Which gas in the air is needed for burning?
hints: It is the gas we breathe in to live.
questions.explanation: Oxygen is the gas in the air that is needed for burning.
questions.misconception: Carbon dioxide supports burning.

questions.stem: Which gas in the air supports burning?
hints: It is also needed for breathing.
It makes up part of the air.
questions.explanation: Oxygen in the air supports burning.
questions.misconception: Nitrogen supports burning.

questions.stem: Why does a fire need air?
options: Because air contains oxygen which supports burning
questions.explanation: A fire needs air because air contains oxygen, which supports burning.
questions.misconception: Air is not needed for burning.

questions.stem: What happens to a fire when it is deprived of air?
hints: Without air, the fire cannot continue.
questions.explanation: A fire goes out when deprived of air because it needs oxygen to keep burning.
questions.misconception: Fire burns without air.

questions.stem: Explain why air is necessary for burning.
answer: air contains oxygen which is needed for burning
oxygen in the air supports burning
fire needs oxygen from the air to burn
hints: What gas in air supports burning?
questions.explanation: Air is necessary for burning because it contains oxygen, which is needed for a fire to burn.
questions.misconception: Air is not needed for burning.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'A fire will burn forever if it has fuel.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, fuel is all a fire needs
No, a fire also needs oxygen from the air to keep burning
No, a fire needs water to keep burning
No, a fire needs sand to keep burning
hints: Without oxygen, the fire goes out.
questions.explanation: A fire needs both fuel and oxygen. Without oxygen from the air, the fire will go out.
questions.misconception: Fuel alone is enough for burning.

questions.stem: A burning candle is covered with a glass jar. What happens after a short time?
hints: The candle uses up the oxygen.
questions.explanation: When a burning candle is covered with a glass jar, the flame goes out because the candle uses up the oxygen inside the jar.
questions.misconception: The candle continues to burn in the jar.

questions.stem: Why does the candle flame go out when covered with a glass jar?
options: The oxygen inside the jar is used up
The candle runs out of wax
hints: The jar traps the air, and the oxygen is used up.
questions.explanation: The candle flame goes out because the burning candle uses up the oxygen inside the jar. Without oxygen, the flame cannot continue.
questions.misconception: The jar is cold, so the flame goes out.

questions.stem: In the candle-and-jar experiment, why does the flame go out?
answer: the candle uses up the oxygen in the jar
the oxygen inside the jar is used up
there is no more oxygen for burning
questions.explanation: The flame goes out because the candle uses up the oxygen trapped inside the jar, and fire cannot burn without oxygen.
questions.misconception: The jar blocks the flame physically.

questions.stem: In groups, carry out the candle-and-jar experiment. Light a candle, cover it with a glass jar, and observe what happens. Describe your observation and explain why it happens.

criteria.description: Observed that the candle flame goes out when covered
Explained that the candle uses up the oxygen in the jar

questions.explanation: This is a practical task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: The candle continues to burn.

questions.stem: Why is air important for burning?
options: It contains oxygen which supports burning
questions.explanation: Air is important for burning because it contains oxygen, which supports burning.
questions.misconception: Air is not important for burning.

questions.stem: Why is air important for burning?
answer: it contains oxygen which supports burning
oxygen in air is needed for burning
questions.explanation: Air is important for burning because it contains oxygen, which is needed for fire to burn.
questions.misconception: Air has no effect on fire.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'Air is only important for breathing.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, air is only for breathing
No, air is also important for burning because it contains oxygen
No, air is only important for plants
No, air is not important at all
questions.explanation: Air is important for breathing and also for burning because it contains oxygen.
questions.misconception: Air is only for breathing.

questions.stem: If you cover a burning candle with a jar, what will happen?
options: The flame will move out of the jar
questions.explanation: The flame will go out because the candle uses up the oxygen inside the jar.
questions.misconception: The flame continues to burn.

questions.stem: Predict what happens if you blow gently on a small flame.
answer: the flame may go out because the air blows it away
hints: Blowing removes the air around the flame.
What happens when you blow out a candle?
questions.explanation: Blowing gently on a small flame can put it out because it removes the air around the flame and the burning gases are blown away.
questions.misconception: Blowing always makes a fire bigger.

questions.stem: A learner fans a glowing charcoal fire with a piece of cardboard. What happens and why?
options: The fire glows brighter because more oxygen is supplied
The fire goes out because air is removed
questions.explanation: Fanning the fire supplies more oxygen from the air, which makes the fire glow brighter.
questions.misconception: Fanning always puts out a fire.

questions.stem: Which of these shows that air supports burning?
options: Blowing on a fire to make it burn brighter
hints: Blowing adds more air to the fire.
questions.explanation: Blowing on a fire to make it burn brighter shows that air (oxygen) supports burning.
questions.misconception: Blowing always puts out a fire.

questions.stem: Give one everyday example showing that air supports burning.
answer: blowing on a fire to make it burn brighter
using a fan to make a fire burn
opening a window to let air in for a fire
hints: Think about what makes a fire burn better.
questions.explanation: An everyday example is blowing on a fire or fanning it to make it burn brighter, because fresh air supplies more oxygen.
questions.misconception: Air does not affect fire.

questions.stem: Why does covering a fire with a blanket put it out?
options: It cuts off the air and oxygen supply to the fire
It makes the fire too hot
It adds fuel to the fire
It blows air into the fire
questions.explanation: Covering a fire with a blanket puts it out because the blanket cuts off the air and oxygen supply needed for burning.
questions.misconception: Blankets add air to a fire.
